From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Contra, contrà, and contra-

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from Latin contrā.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈkɒntɹə/
  • (General American) IPA(key): /ˈkɑntɹə/
  • Audio (US):(file)

Preposition

[edit]

contra

  1. Against; contrary or opposed to; in opposition or contrast to.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • against, anti

Antonyms

[edit]
  • for, pro

Related terms

[edit]
  • contra-
  • contra proferentem
  • per contra
  • semen contra

Translations

[edit]
against, contrary or opposed to
  • Bulgarian: против (bg) (protiv)
  • German: gegen (de), im Gegensatz zu m, contra (de), anti, wider (de)
  • Latin: contrā (la)
  • Old English: aġēn
  • Polish: kontra (pl)
  • Swedish: kontra (sv)
  • Tagalog: kontra

Adverb

[edit]

contra (comparative more contra, superlative most contra)

  1. Contrary to something.
    • 1893 November 30, “The W.C.T.U. Convention. Interesting Reports Considered in Relation to the Several Departments of the Work. Suggested Lines of Development—Programme for the Closing Day.”, in The Daily Colonist, volume LXX, number 148, Victoria, B.C., page 3, column 1:
      […] it is useless to pray “Thy kingdom come” and vote contra or stay away from the polls; […]

Synonyms

[edit]
  • See also Thesaurus:contrarily

Translations

[edit]
contrary to something
  • Arabic: عَلَى اَلْعَكْس (ʕalā l-ʕaks), عَلَى اَلنَّقِيض مِن (ʕalā n-naqīḍ min), ضِد (ḍid)
    Egyptian Arabic: عكس (ʕakss), ضد (ḍeḍ)
  • Bulgarian: напротив (bg) (naprotiv), наопаки (bg) (naopaki)
  • German: gegen (de), im Gegensatz zu m, contra (de), gegnerisch (de), gegengesetzt, entgegengesetzt (de)
  • Polish: wbrew (pl)
  • Romanian: împotrivă (ro), contra (ro)

Noun

[edit]

contra (plural contras)

  1. (business) A deal to swap goods or services.
  2. (politics, derogatory) A conservative; originally tied to Nicaraguan counter-revolutionaries.
  3. (accounting, often attributive) An entry (or account) that cancels another entry (or account).
    Synonym: counterentry
    a contra position; a contra entry
    The sum for each contra account is shown in the last column.
  4. (music, informal) Any of the musical instruments in the contrabass range, e.g. contrabassoon, contrabass clarinet or, especially, double bass.
  5. (dance) A contra dance.
  6. (obsolete, US, New England, dance) A country dance.
    • 2001, Ellen Koskoff, editor, The Garland Encyclopedia of World Music: North America, Garland Publishing, page 232:
      Folk histories record that contras were gradually displaced by the introduction of the quadrille and the new couple dances.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • anticontra

Translations

[edit]
(business) a deal to swap goods or services
(accounting) an entry (or account) that cancels another entry
  • Dutch: contrarekening f
  • Finnish: vasta- (fi) (in compounds), vastatili (account), vastakirjaus (entry)
  • German: Gegenkonto (de) n, Gegenbuchung f, Gegenposition f, Gegenrechnung f, Kreditseite f
  • Polish: no equivalent term in Polish, but see konto wykluczające inne konto n
(dance) a contra dance
  • German: Contra Tanz m, Kontratanz m

Verb

[edit]

contra (third-person singular simple present contras, no present participle, no simple past or past participle)

  1. (accounting) To undo; to reverse.
    to contra a position (an entry)

Translations

[edit]
(accounting) to undo an entry
  • German: zurückbuchen, ristornieren, stornieren (de)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Cantor, Carnot, Carton, Catron, TRACON, cantor, carton, corant, craton, tracon

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    From Proto-Italic *komterād, ablative singular feminine of *komteros (“the other of the two who meet, opposite”). The ablative singular masculine/neuter of the same is continued in Latin contrō-, cognate to Oscan contrud. Ultimately from *kom- + *-teros; thus, a doublet of cum, comparable to the relation between intrā and in, and extrā and ex, but unlike these lacking external cognates, and therefore of Italic origin.[1]

    The change from instrumental/ablative to accusative is caused by *-teros used adverbially.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈkɔn.traː]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈkɔn.tra]

    Adverb

    [edit]

    contrā (not comparable)

    1. against
    2. opposite to
    3. contrary to
    4. otherwise
    5. in return, back

    Preposition

    [edit]

    contrā (+ accusative)

    1. against
    2. across from, opposite

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • contrārius

    Postposition

    [edit]

    contrā (+ ablative)

    1. from the opposite direction of, on the opposite side of

    Further reading

    • “contra”, in Charlton T. Lewis (1891), An Elementary Latin Dictionary, New York: Harper & Brothers
    • "contra", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)

      • to contradict some one: dicere contra aliquem or aliquid (not contradicere alicui)

    Preposition

    [edit]

    contra

    1. against, versus

    Adverb

    [edit]

    contra

    1. against, opposed to, opposite
    2. in exchange for

    Spanish

    [edit]
    Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
    contra
    Wikipedia es

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Inherited from Latin contrā. Old Spanish had cuentra as well, with diphthongization of stressed Latin /ŏ/. As the word was generally atonic, the unstressed variant contra prevailed over time.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): (preposition) /kontɾa/ [kõn̪.t̪ɾa]
      • Rhymes: -ontɾa
    • IPA(key): (noun, adverb) /ˈkontɾa/ [ˈkõn̪.t̪ɾa]
      • Audio (Latin America):(file)
      • Rhymes: -ontɾa
      • Syllabification: con‧tra[1][2]

    Preposition

    [edit]

    contra

    1. against, versus
      Synonym: en oposición a
      Antonym: a favor de
      la lucha contra el prejuicio
      the fight against prejudice
      • 2021 August 3, Jill Martin, “EE.UU. supera a España y avanza a semifinales del baloncesto masculino”, in CNN en Español‎[4]:
        La selección masculina de baloncesto de EE.UU. avanzó a las semifinales de los Juegos Olímpicos con una victoria por 95-81 contra España.
        (please add an English translation of this quotation)
